hourly.summary: Arsenal fans are in full tactical nerd mode — dissecting midfield hierarchies (Rice, Lewis-Skelly, Bruno, Ødegaard), debating Zubimendi's minutes and mentality, and fretting over an attack that's 'still a puzzle' despite Madueke links. Refereeing grievances ('should've had a penalty today') sit alongside genuine warmth — one supporter sharing how Arsenal bonded him and his estranged brother — while opposition managers (hello, Hull City) fume at Arteta's lot. No crisis, just the usual high-stakes overthinking with a side of banana-based away-end banter.

daily.summary: Arsenal fan sentiment showed a clear upward trajectory throughout the day, rising from early-morning hopeful speculation (7/10) through pre-match banterous confidence (8/10) to post-match optimism (8/10) and finally smug triumph (9/10) after a 1-0 win over Hull combined with Manchester City's third straight defeat left Arsenal six points clear at the top. The mood shifted from tactical anxiety and 'what if' delusion to outright title-race dominance, fueled by rival collapses and a growing sense that the championship is already Arsenal's to lose.

weekly.summary: The week began with optimism but plunged into crisis after a humiliating Carabao Cup exit to Fleetwood Town, sustaining days of embarrassment and anxious dread ahead of the Anfield clash before culminating in a historic, euphoric 1-0 victory at Liverpool that sent Arsenal top of the table and completed a dramatic emotional redemption. The arc traces a sharp V-shape from pride through embarrassment to triumph. Dominant themes: cup humiliation, Anfield hoodoo anxiety, and ultimate villain-arc conquest.
